messages.subject: Multivariate probit model
parts:
Hi all, I'm new to Nimble and I'm trying to code up a multivariate probit model. 

However, I tried the following parametrisation:

code <- nimbleCode({
  Omega[1:p,1:p] ~ dwish(R[1:p,1:p], 20)
  for(i in 1:n){
    ystar[i, 1:p] ~ dmnorm(zeroes[], cov = Omega[1:p, 1:p])
    y[i, 1:p] <- ystar[i, 1:p] > 0
  }
})

n <- 5; p <- 2
data <- matrix(rbinom(n * p, 1, .5), n, p)

jsdmModel <- nimbleModel(code,
                         data = list(y = data),
                         inits = list(Omega = diag(1, p)),
                         dimensions = list(y = c(n,p),
                                           ystar = c(n,p),
                                           Omega = c(p, p)),
                         constants = list(
                           R = diag(1,p),
                           n = n,
                           p = p,
                           zeroes = rep(0, p)))

pumpConf <- configureMCMC(jsdmModel, print = TRUE)
jsdmcompiled <- compileNimble(jsdmModel, resetFunctions = T)
jsdmConf <- configureMCMC(jsdmcompiled, print = TRUE,
                          monitors = c('Omega'),
                          enableWAIC = T)
jsdmMCMC <- buildMCMC(jsdmConf)

Nimble is able to simulate from the model, but somehow it does not recognize y as data as it does fail saying 

"Error in buildWAIC(model, mvSaved, conf$controlWAIC) : buildWAIC: cannot compute WAIC with no data nodes in the model"

Is this expected and I'm making any mistake in understanding how Nimble works?

Thank you in advance!

Alex

messages.author: bfa4a88c8a5bc54e
messages.subject: Re: Multivariate probit model
parts:
Hi there,

I’m not familiar with this model but I do believe data nodes always have to follow a stochastic declaration. So y had to be distributed (“~”) as something. Currently you have a deterministic declaration. 

Hope this helps. 

Cheers,

Matt

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Multivariate probit model
parts:
Hi Alex,

Matt is right -- data nodes have to be stochastic. What you tried to do should give an error (our documentation for `setData` mentions this), but in light of your post, I see that we have a bug that causes no error to be given. We'll fix that shortly.

It's easy to do what you want in terms of fitting the model, but unfortunately not in terms of getting WAIC.

To specify the model, you can use `dinterval` (or `dconstraint`, but that is a bit more involved) for the elements of `y`, which would be specified as data.

However, this won't work for WAIC. If you introduce the latent 'ystar' variables, you'd need the marginal version of WAIC (see `help(waic)`) to average over the latent variable, but that would do Monte Carlo sampling of 'ystar' from its posterior predictive not conditioning on 'y' , so some of the samples would give a -Inf log probability. If you can specify the probit model with the latent 'ystar', then you could use our standard (conditional) WAIC. But I'm not sure in general of how to get WAIC from the latent variable version of the probit model. 

-chris
